source_text:
Εἰώθασιν γάρ τινες δόλῳ πονηρῷ τὸ ὄνομα περιφέρειν, ἄλλα τινὰ πράσσοντες ἀνάξια θεοῦ: οὕς δεῖ ὑμᾶς ὡς θηρία ἐκκλίνειν: εἰσὶν γὰρ κύνες λυσσῶντες, λαθροδῆκται: οὓς δεῖ ὑμᾶς φυλάσσεσθαι ὄντας δυσθεραπεύτους.
εἷς ἰατρός ἐστιν, σαρκικός τε καὶ πνευματικός, γεννητὸς καὶ ἀγέννητος, ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ θεός, ἐν θανάτῳ ζωὴ ἀληθινή, καὶ ἐκ Μαρίας καὶ ἐκ θεοῦ, πρῶτον παθητὸς καὶ τότε ἀπαθής. Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν.
thought_title: False teachers as rabid dogs; the one physician Jesus Christ
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Ephesian church about false teachers who carry the name of Christ while acting unworthily, and then he confesses the paradoxical identity of Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: For some have been accustomed with evil deceit the name to carry around, other certain things doing unworthy of God: whom it is necessary [for] you as wild beasts to shun: for they are dogs rabid, biting secretly: whom it is necessary [for] you to guard against, being hard to heal. One physician there is, both flesh and spirit, begotten and unbegotten, in man God, in death life true, and from Mary and from God, first passible and then impassible. Jesus Christ the Lord of us.

choices.why: Keeps the two nouns distinct and the adjective with deceit, matching the source's emphasis on the malicious cunning of the false teachers
Preserves the compound's force of hidden attack, which fits the dog metaphor and the warning against covert false teaching
Keeps the medical metaphor that leads directly into the confession of Christ as the one physician
Uses the glossary's flesh language and keeps the paired adjectives as a paradox rather than resolving it
Preserves the exact theological paradox of origin, which is central to Ignatius's anti-docetic point
Uses the glossary's passion language and keeps the temporal sequence explicit, which is the heart of the incarnation claim
rejected: first able to suffer and then unable to suffer
first suffering and then beyond suffering

pass_b_english: Some people, you see, have made a habit of carrying the name around with evil deceit while doing other things unworthy of God. You must shun them as you would wild beasts, for they are mad dogs that bite when you are not looking. Guard yourselves against them, because they are hard to heal.

There is one physician, both flesh and spirit, begotten and unbegotten, God in a human being, true life in death, both from Mary and from God, first subject to suffering and then beyond suffering: Jesus Christ our Lord.

last_rejected.why: "Passible" is archaic/technical; source means capable of suffering, i.e., mortal.
last_rejected.fix: first capable of suffering and then beyond suffering
last_rejected.ruling: παθητὸς means 'capable of suffering'; 'passible' is standard theological term, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: "Impassible" suggests philosophical impassibility, not the resurrection change the source implies.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπαθής means 'incapable of suffering'; 'impassible' is standard theological term, not a meaning change.
